subproblems.title: C¹ local inverse with surjective inverse derivative (inverse function theorem on ℝ^d)
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^d → ℝ^d (Euclid d), V ⊆ ℝ^d open and v₀ ∈ V. Assume Φ is C¹ on V and its derivative DΦ(v₀) is injective. Then there exist open sets V₁, O ⊆ ℝ^d and a map H : ℝ^d → ℝ^d such that v₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V, Φ(v₀) ∈ O, H is C¹ on O, H(O) = V₁, Φ(H(w)) = w for every w ∈ O, and the derivative DH(w) is surjective for every w ∈ O.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid d → Euclid d) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (v₀ : Euclid d), IsOpen V → v₀ ∈ V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ V → Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ v₀) → ∃ (V₁ O : Set (Euclid d)) (H : Euclid d → Euclid d), IsOpen V₁ ∧ IsOpen O ∧ v₀ ∈ V₁ ∧ V₁ ⊆ V ∧ Φ v₀ ∈ O ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 H O ∧ H '' O = V₁ ∧ (∀ w ∈ O, Φ (H w) = w) ∧ ∀ w ∈ O, Surjective (fderiv ℝ H w)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof (selected node local_inverse), steps 2–6 (pointwise regularity, invertible derivative at v₀, persistence of invertibility, inverse function theorem restricted to the invertibility region, C¹ inverse with derivative E_v⁻¹), stated for a general map Φ that is C¹ on an open V ⊆ Euclid d instead of Φ = F ∘ ψ on V₀ ∩ ψ⁻¹(U). Conventions: E := Euclid d; "C¹" means ContDiff(On/At) ℝ 1; DΦ := fderiv ℝ Φ. No import beyond GMT.Ch07.Submission is needed or allowed (a leaf inserts only its theorem); every lemma cited below is available there.
1. (Pointwise regularity.) Since V is open and Φ is C¹ on V, Φ is C¹ at every v ∈ V (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt, using V ∈ 𝓝 v); hence Φ is differentiable at v (ContDiffAt.differentiableAt, 1 ≠ 0) and HasFDerivAt Φ (DΦ(v)) v.
2. (Invertible derivative at v₀.) DΦ(v₀) is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space E, hence bijective. So E₀ := (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo DΦ(v₀) hinj).toContinuousLinearEquiv is a continuous linear equivalence E ≃L[ℝ] E whose coercion to E →L[ℝ] E equals DΦ(v₀) (the two maps agree at every vector by definition). By step 1, HasFDerivAt Φ E₀ v₀.
3. (Invertibility persists.) The map v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous on the open set V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, 1 ≤ 1). The set R of continuous linear maps E →L[ℝ] E that are coercions of continuous linear equivalences E ≃L[ℝ] E is open (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen; E is complete). Hence V₁′ := V ∩ DΦ⁻¹(R) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage), and v₀ ∈ V₁′ because DΦ(v₀) = E₀ by step 2. For every v ∈ V₁′ choose E_v : E ≃L[ℝ] E with E_v = DΦ(v); then HasFDerivAt Φ E_v v by step 1 (v ∈ V).
4. (Inverse function theorem, restricted to V₁′.) By step 1, Φ is C¹ at v₀, so HasStrictFDerivAt Φ DΦ(v₀) v₀ (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt, 1 ≠ 0), i.e. HasStrictFDerivAt Φ E₀ v₀ by step 2. HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph yields an open partial homeomorphism Φ̃ : E → E whose coercion is Φ (HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe) and with v₀ ∈ Φ̃.source (HasStrictFDerivAt.mem_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source). Let Φ₁ := Φ̃.restrOpen V₁′ (V₁′ is open by step 3). Its coercion is still Φ, and Φ₁.source = Φ̃.source ∩ V₁′ (OpenPartialHomeomorph.restrOpen_source). Put V₁ := Φ₁.source, O := Φ₁.target and H := Φ₁.symm. Then V₁ and O are open (open_source, open_target); v₀ ∈ V₁ (as v₀ ∈ Φ̃.source and v₀ ∈ V₁′); V₁ ⊆ V₁′ ⊆ V; Φ(v₀) = Φ₁(v₀) ∈ O (map_source); H '' O = V₁ (symm_image_target_eq_source); and Φ(H w) = Φ₁(Φ₁.symm w) = w for every w ∈ O (right_inv).
5. (H is C¹ with surjective derivative.) Let w ∈ O and v := H w. Then v ∈ Φ₁.source = V₁ ⊆ V₁′ (map_target), so by step 3 there is E_v : E ≃L[ℝ] E with E_v = DΦ(v) and HasFDerivAt Φ₁ E_v v (Φ₁ coerces to Φ), and Φ₁ is C¹ at v by step 1 (v ∈ V). OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm (applied with w ∈ Φ₁.target) shows that H = Φ₁.symm is C¹ at w; as w ∈ O was arbitrary, H is C¹ on O (ContDiffAt.contDiffWithinAt at each point). OpenPartialHomeomorph.hasFDerivAt_symm gives HasFDerivAt H E_v.symm w, hence fderiv ℝ H w = E_v.symm (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), which is surjective because E_v.symm is an equivalence.
6. (Conclusion.) V₁, O and H satisfy: V₁ and O are open, v₀ ∈ V₁ ⊆ V, Φ(v₀) ∈ O, H is C¹ on O, H '' O = V₁, and Φ(H w) = w and DH(w) is surjective for every w ∈ O. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pointwise: Φ is C¹ and differentiable at every v ∈ V (V open), with HasFDerivAt Φ (DΦ v) v.
DΦ(v₀) is an injective endomorphism of the finite-dimensional E, so it is the coercion of E₀ : E ≃L[ℝ] E (LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, toContinuousLinearEquiv).
Invertibility persists on the open set V₁′ := V ∩ DΦ⁻¹(range of the coercion from E ≃L[ℝ] E), which contains v₀ (continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, ContinuousLinearEquiv.isOpen, isOpen_inter_preimage).

HasStrictFDerivAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph (via ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt) restricted to V₁′ (restrOpen) gives V₁ := source ∋ v₀, O := target ∋ Φ v₀ and H := symm, with V₁ ⊆ V, H '' O = V₁ and Φ ∘ H = id on O.
At each w ∈ O, contDiffAt_symm makes H C¹ at w and hasFDerivAt_symm gives fderiv ℝ H w = E_v.symm with v = H w, which is surjective.

subproblems.title: Images of open subsets under a proper injective chart are relatively open
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, M, W ⊆ ℝ^P, V, V₁ ⊆ ℝ^d and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume W is open, ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, V₁ is open and V₁ ⊆ V. Then there is an open set N₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with M ∩ N₀ = ψ(V₁).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (M W : Set (Euclid P)) (V V₁ : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), IsOpen W → ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ M → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → IsOpen V₁ → V₁ ⊆ V → ∃ N₀ : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen N₀ ∧ M ∩ N₀ = ψ '' V₁
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof (selected node local_inverse), step 8 (ψ(V₁) is relatively open in M), stated for an arbitrary open V₁ ⊆ V and arbitrary dimensions P, d. Conventions: B_r(x) := ball x r; distances are Euclidean. No import beyond GMT.Ch07.Submission is needed. The accepted lemma Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity is supplied by the sibling reuse child chart_inverse_continuity, listed in depends_on so that it is merged into this leaf's Lean base.
1. (ψ(V) ⊆ W.) ψ(V) = W ∩ M ⊆ W.
2. (Local radii.) Let v ∈ V₁. As V₁ is open, choose ε_v > 0 with B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Apply the accepted lemma Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity to P, d, V, W, ψ (ψ is continuous and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W by step 1, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W), to the point v ∈ V (since V₁ ⊆ V) and to ε_v > 0: this gives δ_v > 0 such that every v′ ∈ V with dist(ψ v′, ψ v) < δ_v satisfies dist(v′, v) < ε_v, hence v′ ∈ B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁. Choose such δ_v for all v ∈ V₁ simultaneously (in Lean, `choose` on the statement ∀ v ∈ V₁, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ v′ ∈ V, dist (ψ v′) (ψ v) < δ → v′ ∈ V₁; then δ_v depends on the proof of v ∈ V₁).
3. (Definition of N₀.) Put N₀ := ⋃_{v ∈ V₁} (W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v)). Each W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) is open (W is open and balls are open), so N₀ is open (isOpen_iUnion applied to the outer union over v and to the inner union over the proof of v ∈ V₁).
4. (M ∩ N₀ ⊆ ψ(V₁).) Let x ∈ M with x ∈ W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) for some v ∈ V₁. Then x ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), so x = ψ(v′) for some v′ ∈ V, and dist(ψ v′, ψ v) < δ_v. By step 2, v′ ∈ V₁, so x = ψ(v′) ∈ ψ(V₁).
5. (ψ(V₁) ⊆ M ∩ N₀.) Let v ∈ V₁. Then v ∈ V, so ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ M; thus ψ(v) ∈ M and ψ(v) ∈ W, and ψ(v) ∈ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) because δ_v > 0. Hence ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) ⊆ N₀, so ψ(v) ∈ M ∩ N₀.
6. (Conclusion.) N₀ is open and, by steps 4 and 5, M ∩ N₀ = ψ(V₁). ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ(V) ⊆ W because ψ(V) = W ∩ M.
For each v ∈ V₁, take ε_v with B_{ε_v}(v) ⊆ V₁ and δ_v > 0 from the accepted Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity, so v′ ∈ V and dist(ψ v′, ψ v) < δ_v imply v′ ∈ V₁.
N₀ := ⋃_{v ∈ V₁} (W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v)) is open (isOpen_iUnion twice).
M ∩ N₀ ⊆ ψ(V₁): a point of M ∩ W ∩ B_{δ_v}(ψ v) is ψ(v′) with v′ ∈ V (W ∩ M = ψ(V)) and then v′ ∈ V₁.
ψ(V₁) ⊆ M ∩ N₀: for v ∈ V₁, ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ M and ψ(v) ∈ B_{δ_v}(ψ v).

subproblems.title: Continuity of the inverse of a proper injective chart (Simon Ch. 2, (4.1)–(4.2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every v ∈ V and ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Distances are Euclidean. No openness of V or W is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ W → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → ∀ v ∈ V, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.chart_tangent_space-a1.inverse_continuity-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 5e4b21584624). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. It is cited by step 8 of the supplied proof and is used by the new child chart_image_open, which lists it in depends_on so that the accepted declaration is merged into that leaf's Lean base. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 2, §4, Definition (4.1) and the remark before (4.2) (book/chapter-02.txt, lines 849–862). There Simon notes that "the above definition ensures the local representation is a homeomorphism of V onto the image M ∩ W"; the properness condition of (4.1) is what makes this work. This child is step 2 of the parent proof (node chart_tangent_space), restricted to the hypotheses that step actually uses. Openness of V and W is not needed. Distances are Euclidean.
Fix v ∈ V and ε > 0, and write q := ψ(v).
1. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no δ > 0 has the stated property. Then for every j ∈ ℕ the number δ = 1/(j+1) > 0 fails. So there is v_j ∈ V with |ψ(v_j) − q| < 1/(j+1) and |v_j − v| ≥ ε.
2. We have 0 ≤ |ψ(v_j) − q| < 1/(j+1) and 1/(j+1) → 0. By squeezing, ψ(v_j) → q as j → ∞.
3. Let K := {q} ∪ {ψ(v_j) : j ∈ ℕ}. K is compact because it is the range of a convergent sequence together with its limit. Indeed, given an open cover of K, one member contains q, and by step 2 it contains ψ(v_j) for all j ≥ j₀. Finitely many further members cover ψ(v_0), …, ψ(v_{j₀−1}).
4. K ⊆ W. For each j, v_j ∈ V, so ψ(v_j) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W. Also v ∈ V, so q = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ W.
5. By the properness hypothesis applied to the compact set K ⊆ W, the set C := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact. Every v_j lies in C, because v_j ∈ V and ψ(v_j) ∈ K. C is a compact subset of the metric space ℝ^d, hence sequentially compact. So there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a point v* ∈ C with v_{φ(i)} → v* as i → ∞. In particular v* ∈ V.
6. Now v* ∈ V, every v_{φ(i)} lies in V, and v_{φ(i)} → v*. Since ψ is continuous on V, it is continuous at v* relative to V, so ψ(v_{φ(i)}) → ψ(v*). On the other hand, (ψ(v_{φ(i)}))_i is a subsequence of (ψ(v_j))_j, so ψ(v_{φ(i)}) → q by step 2. Limits in ℝ^P are unique, hence ψ(v*) = q = ψ(v).
7. Both v* and v lie in V, and ψ is injective on V, so v* = v. Thus v_{φ(i)} → v. Hence |v_{φ(i)} − v| < ε for some i. This contradicts step 1, which gives |v_j − v| ≥ ε for every j, in particular for j = φ(i).
8. So the assumption in step 1 is false. There is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Since v ∈ V and ε > 0 were arbitrary, the statement is proved.
proof_key_steps: Negating the claim gives v_j ∈ V with |ψ(v_j) − ψ(v)| < 1/(j+1) and |v_j − v| ≥ ε, so ψ(v_j) → ψ(v).
K = {ψ(v)} ∪ {ψ(v_j)} is compact and lies in W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact and contains every v_j.
A subsequence v_{φ(i)} converges to some v* ∈ V. Continuity of ψ on V and uniqueness of limits give ψ(v*) = ψ(v).
Injectivity on V gives v* = v, which contradicts |v_{φ(i)} − v| ≥ ε.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.chart_tangent_space-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit d626082a69a0). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. It is cited by steps 1 and 7 of the supplied proof (tangentSpace M (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) for every v ∈ V₀, applied with d := 2, r := 1, N := M to the chart (V₀, W₀, ψ) at p) and is used directly by the parent assembly; as a child, its accepted history (which also contains Submission.dsmc_chart_inverse_continuity) is merged into the parent's Lean base. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used in steps 3 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).
